To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TBTs imposed both at home and abroad matter for FDI.
(1) the presence of TBTs in a host country increases FDI inflows, and (2) FDI outflows from a country with more TBTs are larger.
the STCs raised on TBTs imposed in the CESEE region by the host economies stimulate inward FDI, while the TBTs in the home countries of EU28 investors have a positive effect on their outward FDI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the CESEE countries are TBT havens for EU28 MNEs or TBT jumpers for non EU28 MNE investors.
the impact of TBTs on the FDI stocks in CESEE countries and the role of home country regulations and standards.
the question whether MNEs invest in countries that impose TBTs that are more or less restrictive than the home country's.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TBTs are more likely to stimulate than to hamper FDI.
TBTs are not always barriers to trade and FDI.
TBTs imposed in host countries stimulate FDI stocks in CESEE countries, while TBTs in the home country have a negative effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EU28 MNEs are attracted to the CESEE economies by the quality TBTs that are imposed by the CESEE countries, whereas the non EU28 MNE are attracted by the quality T BTs imposed by the CESEEs themselves.
TBTs are not always a barrier to trade and investment, but rather they might be used as a means of attracting FDI to a country.
TBTs can be both a barrier and an incentive for foreign direct investment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MNEs from the EU28 and non-EU28 countries respond differently to the TBTs.
MNEs' FDI decisions are influenced by the regulatory environment of the host countries, and this influence is not uniform across different types of regulations.
TBTs can be a double-edged sword: while they might have positive externalities and improve market efficiencies, they might also be used as barriers to trade and investment.
